data.narrative:
Gauss Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised €9M to date. The valuation landscape for frontier nuclear technology remains sparse: the relevant peer universe comprises 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Fuse Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and General Matter. However, this broader set does not provide sufficient granularity for robust valuation triangulation.

The Peer-Median method, typically a primary valuation anchor, is not applicable here. Only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage nuclear energy company with available data could be identified; the standard requirement of three or more comparable datapoints cannot be met within tight stage and sector filters. Attempting to apply all-sector median multiples would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of nuclear technology risk profiles and capital requirements across the peer set. The small number of mature public comparables further limits the ability to establish reliable revenue or EBITDA multiples specific to early-stage nuclear development.

Without sufficient comparable transaction data or public market multiples applicable at Series A, this analysis cannot support a quantitative valuation range. Key uncertainties include technology maturity relative to peers, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity through commercialization. A credible valuation would require either access to recent Series A+ pricing in the nuclear sector, or application of cost-of-capital and scenario-based DCF methods leveraging company-specific technical and market assumptions—neither of which is available in the current dataset.
